abstract: ABSTRACT Prior research on user innovation fails to explain its low adoption rate and neglects its impact on increased product stickiness. To bridge these gaps, we conducted an empirical investigation into user innovations within the video game sector. Our study reveals that embracing user innovation leads to an upsurge in the number of active players for a game. Furthermore, the marginal effect of user innovations varies depending on their recency and quality , with low‐quality user innovations leading to user attrition. The effect is also contingent on the stage in the product life cycle in which user innovation is adopted.
abstract_zh: 摘要 先前关于用户创新的研究未能解释其低采纳率，并忽视了其对产品粘性增强的影响。为弥补这些空白，我们对视频游戏行业的用户创新进行了实证调查。研究发现，采纳用户创新能显著提升游戏的活跃玩家数量。此外，用户创新的边际效应因其新颖性和质量而异，低质量的用户创新会导致用户流失。该效应还取决于用户创新被采纳时所处的产品生命周期阶段。
title: User Innovation and Product Stickiness: Evidence From Video Games
title_zh: 用户创新与产品粘性：来自视频游戏的证据

abstract: Inclusive urban growth in many developing countries hinges on how effectively rural–urban migrants integrate into host cities. Although social integration dynamically unfolds over time and rural–urban dual homeownership – holding both urban residential properties and rural homesteads – is common amid rapid structural change, its implications for the dynamics of integration remain unclear. Using a nationally representative survey of migrants in China and a two-step control function approach, we examine how dual homeownership shapes social integration measured along three evolving dimensions. We find that urban homeownership markedly enhances migrants’ social integration, whereas retaining rural homesteads weakens it. These patterns are robust to a set of alternative estimation strategies and are heterogeneous across city sizes and urban housing property types. Mechanism analyses suggest that the benefits of urban homeownership operate primarily through residential stability, while the adverse effect of retaining rural homesteads reflects a persistent psychological attachment to origin villages. In contrast, financial channels – such as mortgage burdens associated with urban homeownership and liquidity constraints from retaining rural homesteads – play a limited role. The results point to urban housing policies that strengthen migrants’ residential stability and rural land policies that delink migrant families from their homesteads.

title: The impact of rural–urban dual homeownership on migrants’ social integration in Chinese cities

abstract: While information technology (IT) development enhances productivity, it may also negatively affect low-skilled employment by displacing migrant workers through substitution, productivity, and job creation effects. Using data from the 2015–2017 China Migrants Dynamic Survey (CMDS) and a double machine learning (DML) model, this study examines the impact of IT development at the province-industry level on migrant workers’ overtime work. Results show that IT development significantly increases overtime work, particularly among male, low-skilled, and married workers. This effect operates through reduced hourly wages, higher unemployment risks, and shifts towards self-employment. The findings suggest that IT may exacerbate labour market inequality. Policy responses should include targeted IT training with financial support, improved educational access for migrants’ children, and stronger protections for self-employed workers.

abstract: This paper studies the effect of government procurement on corporate employment by utilizing the combination of government contracts and listed company data. Our study demonstrates that government procurement exerts a significant promoting effect on corporate employment. This effect is more pronounced in firms with higher financial constraints, and firms in the growth cycle. Mechanism tests show that liquidity constraints and credit access serve as two critical mechanisms. Further analysis shows that corporate employment is typically influenced by the procurements that come from central government, local government and sustained procurements. Besides, government procurement significantly raises firms’ investment, human capital and sales revenue. Our findings shed light on how fiscal and stimulus policies increase employment and investment.
title: Government procurement and corporate employment
